vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: structs-combat
Version: 1.1.1

The skill bundle provides instructions for an AI agent to perform combat and raiding operations within a game environment using the 'structsd' CLI tool. The content in SKILL.md is entirely focused on game mechanics such as fleet movement, Proof-of-Work (PoW) raid computation, and defensive formations, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized system access.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions directly perform live combat/raid transactions and require access to local CLI keys and significant background CPU for PoW, but the skill declares no credentials or config access — that mismatch is suspicious and needs clarification before use.

dimensions.detail: The name and description (combat/raids/defense) match the SKILL.md commands (structsd tx ...). However the runtime commands implicitly require access to local account keys, a running structsd client, network access to submit transactions, and local config/keyrings; none of these capabilities or config paths/credentials are declared in the skill metadata. That omission is a coherence concern.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent/operator to run structsd CLI transactions (attacks, fleet moves, planet-raid-compute that performs PoW and auto-submits). These are state-changing, externally-visible actions and may consume significant CPU for background PoW. The instructions do not ask to read arbitrary system files, but they do assume access to private keys (via --from [key-name]) and the structsd runtime environment; this is a material scope requirement that is not surfaced in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — low installation risk (nothing written to disk by the skill itself).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or config paths, yet its runbook requires using --from [key-name] (private keys/keyring) and a running structsd instance with network access. The absence of declared credentials/config access is disproportionate. Additionally, the planet-raid-compute step requires background PoW hashing which may consume substantial CPU; that resource and uptime requirement is not declared.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true', does not install anything, and does not modify other skills or system-wide agent config according to the provided files. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not combined here with elevated persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will instruct the agent/operator to run live structsd transactions (attacks, raids) that require a local structsd client, network access, and private keys (specified with --from [key-name]) and will run a CPU‑heavy PoW step for raids. Before installing or running it: 1) Confirm where your structsd keys live (keyring, ~/.config, hardware wallet) and never expose private keys to an agent you don't fully trust. 2) Don’t run planet-raid-compute on shared or critical machines — it can use high CPU for minutes–hours. 3) Ask the skill author to explicitly declare required config paths and credential types (keyring locations or environment variables) and to document what actions are live vs. simulated/test. 4) If you intend to test, run in a sandbox or testnet account with throwaway keys. 5) Consider legal/ethical implications of automated attack/raid actions in the target environment. The mismatch between declared metadata (no creds/config) and required runtime access is the primary reason to treat this skill with caution.
